evals.prompt: A collaborator uses either Claude Code or Codex in this repository. I want the latest remote changes before work. Can we just tell the agent once instead of making a launcher or a large synchronization service?
evals.expected_output: Routes to the session-routine path: a natural-language or project-instruction workflow, git pull --ff-only on a clean worktree only, no auto-stash/merge/rebase/overwrite, and no hook proposed since pre-prompt timing wasn't required.
expectations: Does not propose a launcher, shortcut, or custom synchronization daemon
Uses project instructions or a normal agent request as the default mechanism, per the 'least mechanism' operating principle
Preserves dirty/diverged work rather than auto-stashing or force-overwriting
Does not propose a lifecycle hook for this ordinary sync request

evals.prompt: I see the same SessionStart message three times. Find out why and tell me what to change. Do not assume there are three registrations.
evals.expected_output: Routes to hook-diagnosis mode: audits all hook scopes and correlates firings with root/resume/compact/subagent sessions before editing anything, rather than assuming duplicate configuration.
expectations: Counts actual hook registrations before changing any configuration
Correlates each observed firing with its lifecycle source or agent session rather than guessing
States a verified root cause (not an assumption) before proposing a fix

evals.prompt: This TypeScript repository has package.json and package-lock.json, no Python files, and no ONBOARDING.md. Help me get it running.
evals.expected_output: Routes to environment-repair mode: detects the real stack from the lockfile, uses npm, and verifies the project's own start/test path rather than inventing requirements or a new onboarding doc.
expectations: Detects npm specifically from package-lock.json rather than defaulting to another package manager
Does not require Python, uv, ffmpeg, or a .env file the repo never declared
Does not stop to ask whether to create ONBOARDING.md when nothing indicates one is needed
Verifies success via the project's actual start/test command, not just 'dependencies installed'

evals.prompt: I explicitly need a dynamic setup reminder injected before the first Claude Code prompt. Install it without touching my existing PreToolUse hooks, and make sure resume and compact do not fire it.
evals.expected_output: Routes to startup-automation mode (genuine pre-prompt timing requirement): passes the hook gate, previews the change, preserves unrelated settings, installs one SessionStart group with matcher startup, and documents removal.
expectations: Uses matcher 'startup' specifically so resume/compact do not also fire it
Preserves unrelated existing settings, including the existing PreToolUse hooks
Previews the change before applying it and documents how to remove it
Does not silently duplicate an already-existing managed entry

evals.prompt: I found a hardcoded AWS key in the last commit I made locally but haven't pushed yet. Help me clean this up.
evals.expected_output: Routes to git-safety mode: reads the git-safety reference before any mutation, and handles this as a guarded workflow (e.g. amend or interactive history edit on an unpushed commit) rather than jumping straight to a destructive rewrite without safeguards.
expectations: Recognizes this as a git-safety scenario, not an ordinary sync/environment-repair request
Does not silently force-push or rewrite shared history without first checking whether the commit was ever pushed
Explains the actual remediation step clearly before performing it

evals.prompt: A new teammate is joining next week and needs to get productive on this repo fast. What's missing from our onboarding?
evals.expected_output: Routes to repository-handoff mode: audits what onboarding material already exists and fills only the genuinely missing operational contract, rather than writing a full onboarding doc from scratch regardless of what's already there.
expectations: Checks for existing onboarding material (README, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING, etc.) before proposing new content
Identifies specific, concrete gaps rather than a generic 'you should have better docs' response
Does not duplicate content that already exists elsewhere in the repo

evals.prompt: Just set up a quick launcher script so I don't have to remember to say 'sync the remote' every time I start working.
evals.expected_output: Declines to build a bespoke launcher/wizard for something a plain natural-language request or project instruction already covers, per the skill's explicit 'do not infer competence from role, do not invent a launcher unless asked with genuine justification' principle — while still explaining the lighter-weight alternative.
expectations: Does not simply build the requested launcher script without first surfacing the lighter-weight project-instruction alternative
Explains why the least-mechanism approach is preferred here
If the user insists after hearing the tradeoff, respects that — this is about not defaulting to heavy mechanism, not refusing outright

evals.prompt: This Python repo has requirements.txt AND a pyproject.toml with different dependency lists, and the previous person on this project isn't around to ask. Get it running.
evals.expected_output: Routes to environment-repair mode, and specifically surfaces the conflicting dependency declarations as a real finding rather than silently picking one file and ignoring the discrepancy.
expectations: Notices and reports the conflicting dependency sources rather than silently choosing one without comment
Bases the choice (or the question back to the user) on real evidence from the repo, not a guess
Still attempts to get a working environment rather than stalling entirely on the ambiguity
